title: Governance, Institutions & Policy Lifecycle Atlas
purpose: Give the World layer a neutral governance grammar for describing how public authority is constituted, constrained, exercised, implemented, reviewed and changed without turning the Room into a partisan scorecard.
master_rule: Describe institutions, authority, procedures, incentives, outcomes and evidence separately. A governance record should make disagreement inspectable rather than hide it inside one overall rating.

questions: What establishes authority?
What rights/competences are entrenched?
How can the basic order be amended?
Who makes general rules?
How are members selected?
How are committees, budgets and oversight organized?
Who directs administration and policy execution?
How are appointments, emergency powers and delegated authority bounded?
How are disputes adjudicated?
What review powers exist?
How are independence, appointment and enforcement structured?
Which bodies implement policy?
What professional, budgetary and procedural capacities do they possess?
What market/social domain is regulated?
What legal mandate, independence, accountability and appeal structure apply?
Which powers/resources belong to regional/local levels?
Which responsibilities are shared or delegated?
What service/capability is delivered?
Who controls it?
How are budgets, performance and accountability handled?
How are candidates/leadership selected?
What commitments, coalition terms and legislative positions are documented?
How can citizens, associations, journalists and interest groups participate, scrutinize or contest public decisions?

authority_dimensions.meaning: How office-holders or decision-makers enter authority.
What the actor is authorized to decide or administer.
Budget, staff, legal powers, information, infrastructure and implementation capacity.
Law, courts, oversight, federal division, transparency, rights, elections, professional rules or external commitments.
Who can demand reasons, review conduct, reverse decisions, sanction failure or replace leadership.
Whether formally adopted decisions can actually be carried out across territory, agencies and time.
How outcomes, public response, audit, data and judicial/administrative review alter future decisions.

measurement_vector.note: Who can participate, compete, petition, access information or organize; method and population must be named.
Whether rules and decisions are subject to known procedures, rights and review mechanisms.
Administrative, fiscal, informational and operational ability to implement lawful decisions.
Availability and effectiveness of answerability, oversight, appeal, audit and replacement mechanisms.
Observed outputs/outcomes in the policy domain; do not infer institutional quality from one outcome alone.
Rules/processes addressing conflicts of interest, misuse of office, procurement and public resources.
Distribution of authority and ability to coordinate across government levels and agencies.
Capacity to revise policy after evidence, shocks, court decisions, audit or changing conditions.

rules: Separate formal rules from observed practice.
Separate policy announcement from authorization, funding, implementation and measured outcome.
State the time period and jurisdiction for every governance assessment.
Keep perceived-governance indicators distinct from direct administrative measures.
Composite indices are views over underlying indicators, not intrinsic properties of a country.
Preserve uncertainty, methodological changes and margins of error where supplied.

comparative_rule: Compare like institutional functions and explicitly state constitutional, historical, territorial and economic context. Do not convert this atlas into an overall political ranking.

source_frameworks.name: World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators
source_frameworks.use: Reference framework for broad governance dimensions and explicit uncertainty/composite-method cautions.

source_frameworks.name: International IDEA State of Democracy Assessment Framework
source_frameworks.use: Question-led assessment of citizenship/law/rights, representative and accountable government, civil society/participation and democracy beyond the state.

source_frameworks.name: OECD Best Practice Principles for Regulatory Policy — Governance of Regulators
source_frameworks.use: Institutional questions around regulator mandate, independence, accountability and performance.

procedural_facts: The Danish Constitution requires a bill to be considered three times by the Folketing before final adoption.
Committee reporting is part of the ordinary route between readings; after second reading a bill can in some cases return to committee before third reading.
Folketing guidance imposes timing rules between readings and publication of committee reports, with separate provisions for expedited handling.

lifecycle_mapping.revision: amendments and possible renewed committee handling

research_questions: How much did the text change between introduction and final reading?
Which amendments were adopted, rejected or withdrawn?
How much time elapsed between readings and committee publication?
Which committees, ministries and external submissions materially shaped the bill?
institutional_process_cases.boundary: This case describes formal procedure. It does not by itself measure deliberative quality, public influence, policy effectiveness or democratic legitimacy.

observed_sequence: final approval of identical text by Parliament and Council
signature and publication in the Official Journal
procedural_facts: The ordinary legislative procedure is the general rule for adopting EU legislation in the policy areas where it applies.
Parliament and Council act as co-legislators on an equal footing and must approve the same final text.
The procedure can involve up to three readings; conciliation is the final stage if disagreement remains after second reading.
Once formally adopted and signed, legislative acts are published in the Official Journal.

lifecycle_mapping.scrutiny: Parliament committee work and Council consideration
lifecycle_mapping.negotiation: Parliament-Council interinstitutional negotiations, often with Commission participation

research_questions: At which reading was agreement reached?
What changed between Commission proposal and final act?
Which committee and rapporteur handled the file in Parliament?
Which amendments or Council positions changed the final text?
What implementation or transposition obligations follow from the adopted act?
institutional_process_cases.boundary: This case describes institutional procedure. It does not assign a quality score to EU policymaking or imply that all EU acts follow the ordinary legislative procedure.

process_comparison_rule: Compare institutional sequences and observable outputs without turning procedural difference into an overall political ranking. A longer or shorter process is not intrinsically better; evaluate the function, context, safeguards, implementation and outcomes separately.
